scope_assessment: Substantive quantitative fixed-support reconstruction from the exact finite-rank theorem, with an explicit primitive-triple injection and a careful uniform-count versus global-height distinction. Literature report accurately leaves global abc open.
actual_checks: Checked Beukers–Schlickewei Theorem 1.1 applies to the Q-closure of a finitely generated subgroup of (C*)² of rank r and gives 2^(8r+8). Divisible closure and sign torsion are retained.
U_S has rank s; its Cartesian square has rank 2s. Negative valuations allow a/c and b/c. Membership in H implies membership in the larger Q-closure.
For primitive ordered positive triples, a/c is reduced since gcd(a,c)=1, so it fixes a,c and then b. This makes normalization injective and yields 2^(16s+8), without counting scaled triples.

Finite support yields an S-dependent constant after taking a finite maximum, but no height estimate uniform over varying supports. Bounded radical implies finitely many possible supports and hence finitely many primitive triples.
